writers.work: An Exposition of the Old and New Testaments

writers.founderRule: The writer fits: a Particular Baptist who held Scripture inspired, already on the cite list as 'gill'. The problem is the transcription, not the writer.
writers.bestSource: No cleanly licensed transcription was found. The nearest usable copy is HelloAO's JSON (https://bible.helloao.org/api/c/john-gill/{BOOK}/{chapter}.json). It is not on GitHub and would need a mirror branch, and it repeats the same text. Editor: Larry Pierce. All Rightes Reserved, Larry Pierce, Winterbourne, Ontario.' HelloAO's /api/available_commentaries.json gives "licenseUrl": "https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/", and its README says 'no copyright restrictions whatsoever'. writers.coverage: HelloAO: 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 29,707 verses. About 8.8 million words, counted in the MyBible copy of the same text.

writers.accuracy: HelloAO text against scans. Hebrews 11:1 against the 1811 edition (expositionofnewt0003john): 200 of 203 words (98.5%). Galatians 2:16, same volume: 190 of 191 (99.5%). Ruth 1:16 against the 1764 first edition: 77.4%. Psalm 23:1 against the 1765 first edition: 70.9%. The misses in those two are long-s OCR noise, plus the editor's modernising: intreat to entreat, chuse to choose, don't to do not, any thing to anything, and Roman-numeral references such as 'Psal. lxxvii' to 'Psalm 77'. Gill's Latin footnotes are not inline. Matthew 5:3 against the 1746 edition could not be judged because that OCR is too poor (42%). The words are Gill's, lightly modernised.
concerns: Rights: the editor of the only electronic text reserves all rights. HelloAO's public-domain mark is a third party relabelling his edition, so the founder's 'plain statement that it is free' test is not clearly met.

Ways forward: ask Online Bible (Larry Pierce) for written permission, or make a new transcription from the 1809 to 1811 London edition scans, which read well (98.5 to 99.5% even through OCR). Otherwise keep Gill as a cite-only writer.

Rabbinic sources on almost every page. Avoid-list match words occur 6,273 times: Kimchi 3,088, Aben Ezra 2,630, Maimonides 517, Nachmanides 17, Ramban 12, Meyer 7. Gill calls Rashi 'Jarchi', which the list does not match. Talmud, Targum and Zohar together come up about 9,255 times.
Harsh wording: about 369 'papist/popery/popish', 159 'Romish', 127 places tying antichrist to the pope or Rome, 189 'Mahomet/Mohammedan/Turk', 123 'blind/obstinate/wicked Jews'.
Largest of the six works; spelling is modernised, not Gill's own.

writers.work: Notes, Explanatory and Practical (Barnes' Notes): the New Testament, and his own Old Testament volumes on Job, Psalms, Isaiah and Daniel

writers.founderRule: Fits; already on the cite list as 'barnes'. He held the whole Bible as God's word. He was tried for heresy in 1835 over his Notes on Romans (original sin and imputation); his synod suspended him and the 1836 General Assembly restored him. That was a Calvinist doctrinal dispute, not one over Scripture. Leave out the 'whole Bible' Barnes editions (StudyLight, e-Sword, MyBible), which put other men's work under his name. Their Genesis 1:1 note is James G. Murphy's Commentary on Genesis, checked against archive.org criticalexeg00murp (1866), and their Numbers is not Barnes's either. Barnes wrote on only Job, Psalms, Isaiah and Daniel in the Old Testament.

writers.work: The Holy Bible ... with a Commentary and Critical Notes
writers.founderRule: Fits the rule as worded; already on the cite list as 'clarke'. A Methodist who held Scripture as God's word. Two positions the founder should know, which would appear word for word. At Luke 1:35 Clarke calls 'the doctrine of the eternal Sonship of Christ ... anti-scriptural, and highly dangerous'; he affirms Christ's full deity but rejects calling the divine nature 'Son' from eternity. At Genesis 3:1 he argues the tempter was a creature 'of the simia or ape genus', not a snake. He is Arminian and argues against Calvinist readings in places. Nothing needs leaving out unless the founder decides otherwise.
